questions.topic: Page 5: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 5-6 Focus)
questions.questionText: Any point lying on the x-axis must have a y-coordinate equal to 0.
questions.explanationAnswer: By definition, the x-axis is the line where the vertical distance from the origin (y-coordinate) is zero.
questions.explanationQuestion: The question asks for the property of points on the x-axis.

questions.topic: Page 5: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 5-6 Focus)
questions.explanationAnswer: Quadrant I is (+, +), II is (-, +), III is (-, -), and IV is (+, -).
questions.explanationQuestion: Match the quadrant with its corresponding sign convention.
questions.questionText: Match the quadrants in a 2-D Cartesian coordinate system with their corresponding sign conventions for the coordinates (x, y).
